description: Russia formally annexed Crimea from Ukraine on 18 March 2015 following a disputed referendum, triggering immediate Western sanctions and elevating broader European security risk.
source_ref: UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262; BBC News 2014-03-18

description: The Islamic State declared a caliphate across captured territory in Iraq and Syria on 29 June 2014, escalating Middle East instability and oil-market risk.
UK citizens voted 52 % to 48 % to leave the European Union on 23 June 2016, triggering immediate pound sterling collapse and global equity volatility.

event_name: US-China Trade War Escalation – Section 301 Tariffs
description: The US announced Section 301 tariffs on over USD 50 billion of Chinese imports on 22 March 2018, initiating a prolonged tit-for-tat trade war that rattled global supply chains and equity markets.

The United States and China signed Phase One of a bilateral trade agreement on 15 January 2020, partially reducing tariffs and establishing purchase commitments, partially defusing the two-year trade war.

Russian military forces launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, triggering severe energy and commodity shocks, broad Western sanctions, and the largest equity-market impact since COVID-19.

Hamas launched a large-scale offensive against Israel on 7 October 2023, killing approximately 1,200 Israelis. Israel declared war and began a major military response in Gaza, escalating Middle East geopolitical risk.

Houthi forces began systematic attacks on commercial shipping in the Red Sea starting December 2023, forcing major carriers to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope and raising global freight and oil shipping costs.

event_name: US Tariff Escalation on China (Liberation Day)
description: On 2 April 2025 President Trump announced sweeping reciprocal tariffs averaging 34 % on Chinese goods ('Liberation Day'), triggering the worst two-day S&P 500 drawdown since 2020 and fears of a global recession.
source_ref: White House Executive Order Apr 2025; Reuters 2025-04-03

description: Donald Trump defeated Hillary Clinton in the US presidential election on 8 November 2016. Markets initially sold off but quickly reversed as investors anticipated fiscal stimulus and deregulation.

event_name: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) Signed
description: President Trump signed the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on 22 December 2017, reducing the corporate tax rate from 35 % to 21 %, a major boost to S&P 500 earnings expectations.

The longest US government shutdown in history ran from 22 December 2018 to 25 January 2019 (35 days) due to border-wall funding disputes, furloughing 800,000 federal workers and weighing on consumer sentiment.

event_name: Joe Biden Wins US Presidential Election
description: Joe Biden was declared the winner of the US presidential election on 7 November 2020. Markets rallied sharply on expectations of fiscal stimulus while healthcare and clean-energy stocks outperformed.
On 6 January 2021 a mob stormed the US Capitol building while Congress was certifying the 2020 election result, briefly disrupting proceedings and triggering a temporary intraday equity sell-off.

President Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act on 16 August 2022, committing roughly USD 369 billion to clean energy, healthcare, and deficit reduction, boosting clean-energy and EV-related stocks.

Donald Trump won the 2024 US presidential election against Kamala Harris on 5 November 2024. Financial stocks surged on deregulation expectations; clean-energy stocks declined; crypto and defence names rallied.

event_name: US Debt Ceiling Crisis and AAA Downgrade
description: Fitch Ratings downgraded the US long-term credit rating from AAA to AA+ on 1 August 2023, citing fiscal deterioration and repeated debt-ceiling standoffs. The S&P 500 fell roughly 1.4 % on the announcement day.

The Federal Reserve raised the federal funds rate by 25 bps on 16 December 2015, its first rate increase since June 2006, signalling confidence in the US economic recovery post-Global Financial Crisis.
Chinese equity markets collapsed on 24 August 2015 ('Black Monday'), with the Shanghai Composite falling 8.5 %, dragging global markets down and briefly pushing the S&P 500 into correction territory.
The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic on 11 March 2020. The S&P 500 ultimately fell ~34 % from its February 2020 peak before recovering, with the VIX spiking above 80.

event_name: Federal Reserve Emergency Rate Cut to Zero
description: The Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate by 100 bps to 0–0.25 % in an emergency inter-meeting action on 15 March 2020, also launching USD 700 billion in quantitative easing to combat COVID-19 disruption.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported June 2022 CPI at 9.1 % YoY on 13 July 2022, the highest reading in 40+ years, cementing expectations of aggressive Fed tightening and pressuring equity valuations.

event_name: Federal Reserve Aggressive Rate Hike Cycle Begins
description: The Federal Reserve began its most aggressive rate-hike cycle since the 1980s on 16 March 2022, raising rates by 25 bps with 10 additional hikes through July 2023 bringing the target to 5.25–5.50 %.

event_name: US Regional Banking Crisis – Silicon Valley Bank Failure
description: Regulators shut down Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) on 10 March 2023 after a sudden deposit run triggered by rising rate losses on its bond portfolio, sparking contagion fears that led to the rapid closure of Signature Bank.

event_name: Federal Reserve First Rate Cut – Pivot Begins
description: The Federal Reserve cut the federal funds rate by 50 bps on 18 September 2024, beginning its easing cycle after holding at 5.25–5.50 % since July 2023, signalling a soft-landing pivot.

event_name: Global Market Selloff – Yen Carry Trade Unwind
description: On 5 August 2024 global markets experienced a historic single-day volatility spike (VIX peaked above 65) driven by rapid yen appreciation after the Bank of Japan's surprise rate hike unwound the yen carry trade.

event_name: DeepSeek R1 AI Shock (AI Capex Rethink)
description: On 27 January 2025 Chinese AI startup DeepSeek released R1, a model rivalling frontier US LLMs at a fraction of the training cost. NVDA fell ~17 % in a single session, the largest single-day market-cap loss in US history, as investors re-evaluated AI infrastructure spending.
Apple announced the iPhone 7 on 7 September 2016, removing the headphone jack and introducing water resistance; the product cycle drove strong Q1 FY2017 earnings for Apple.

OpenAI launched ChatGPT to the public on 30 November 2022, reaching 1 million users in five days. The launch ignited a broad AI investment cycle and triggered a major re-rating of AI-infrastructure stocks.

Microsoft announced the acquisition of Activision Blizzard for USD 68.7 billion on 18 January 2022, the largest gaming deal in history, pending regulatory clearance eventually completed in October 2023.

event_name: NVIDIA Surpasses USD 1 Trillion Market Cap
description: NVIDIA briefly crossed a USD 1 trillion market capitalisation on 30 May 2023, driven by explosive AI-chip demand following its blockbuster Q1 FY2024 earnings report and blowout Q2 guidance.
Rockstar Games released the first official GTA VI trailer on 5 December 2023, breaking YouTube records with over 93 million views in 24 hours; the game is expected for release in 2025.
source_ref: Rockstar Games Official Trailer Dec 2023; YouTube metrics

description: Apple launched the Vision Pro spatial computing headset on 2 February 2024 at USD 3,499, its first major new product category in a decade, with initial sales described as strong but limited by high price.

OpenAI unveiled GPT-4o ('omni') on 13 May 2024, adding real-time voice and vision capabilities at reduced cost, further accelerating enterprise AI adoption and competitive pressure on incumbent software firms.

event_name: Intel Process Node Setback and Layoffs
description: Intel announced a 15,000-employee layoff and suspension of its dividend on 1 August 2024 after a revenue miss and competitive losses in its foundry business, with shares falling ~26 % on results day.

The Summer Olympics were held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil from 5–21 August 2016. The event faced security and infrastructure concerns but completed successfully; NBC reported record streaming viewership.
The FIFA World Cup was held across Russia from 14 June – 15 July 2018. France won the tournament; it was the most watched World Cup in history at the time with global media reach for major sponsors.
The COVID-delayed Tokyo Olympics ran 23 July – 8 August 2021 without spectators due to pandemic restrictions. The US won the most gold medals; NBCUniversal reported record digital streaming numbers.

The FIFA World Cup was held in Qatar 20 November – 18 December 2022, the first held in the Arab world. Argentina won the final on penalties; Fox Sports and Telemundo recorded record viewership for a US audience.
The Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France from 26 July – 11 August 2024. It was the centennial return of the Games to France; NBC reported record streaming viewership exceeding the Tokyo Games.

event_name: Avengers: Endgame Opens – Record Box Office
description: Marvel Studios' Avengers: Endgame opened globally on 26 April 2019, earning USD 357 million domestically in its opening weekend and ultimately becoming the highest-grossing film in history at USD 2.798 billion.
source_ref: Box Office Mojo; Disney Press Release 2019

description: Super Bowl LVIII on 11 February 2024 (Kansas City Chiefs vs. San Francisco 49ers) drew an average US viewership of 123.4 million on CBS, the most watched US television broadcast in history.

Hurricane Harvey made landfall in Texas on 25 August 2017 as a Category 4 storm, causing catastrophic flooding in Houston. Total economic losses were estimated at USD 125 billion; oil refinery disruptions spiked gasoline prices.
Hurricane Irma struck Florida on 10 September 2017 as a Category 4 storm, one of the most powerful Atlantic hurricanes ever recorded, causing approximately USD 50 billion in damage.

event_name: California Camp Fire – Deadliest Wildfire in State History
description: The Camp Fire burned 153,000 acres in Butte County, California from 8–25 November 2018, destroying the town of Paradise and killing 85 people. It forced Pacific Gas & Electric into bankruptcy.
source_ref: CAL FIRE 2018; PG&E Bankruptcy Filing Jan 2019

description: Australia's Black Summer bushfires burned approximately 18.6 million hectares from September 2019 to March 2020, killing at least 33 people and an estimated 3 billion animals, disrupting tourism and air travel.

event_name: Texas Winter Storm Uri – Power Grid Failure
description: A historic winter storm struck Texas 10–20 February 2021, causing the Texas power grid to fail catastrophically, leaving 4.5 million homes without power. Total economic damage exceeded USD 195 billion.
Hurricane Ian made landfall in southwest Florida on 28 September 2022 as one of the strongest hurricanes to strike the US mainland, causing over USD 100 billion in damage and 150 deaths.

A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck southeastern Turkey and northern Syria on 6 February 2023, killing over 50,000 people and causing economic losses estimated at USD 100+ billion – Turkey's worst disaster in a century.

Wildfires swept through Maui, Hawaii on 8 August 2023, destroying the historic town of Lahaina and killing at least 100 people. It was the deadliest US wildfire in over a century, with damages exceeding USD 5 billion.

Amazon announced the acquisition of Whole Foods Market for USD 13.7 billion on 16 June 2017, sending shockwaves through the grocery and retail sector as competitors' stocks dropped sharply on the same day.

event_name: General Electric Removed from Dow Jones
description: General Electric was removed from the Dow Jones Industrial Average on 26 June 2018 after 110 years as a component, replaced by Walgreens Boots Alliance, reflecting GE's prolonged operational and financial struggles.
source_ref: S&P Dow Jones Indices Press Release 2018-06-19

description: Following two fatal crashes (Lion Air Oct 2018; Ethiopian Airlines Mar 2019), aviation regulators worldwide grounded the Boeing 737 MAX on 13 March 2019. Boeing's stock fell ~11 % that day; total costs exceeded USD 20 billion.

event_name: WeWork IPO Collapse and SoftBank Rescue
description: WeWork withdrew its IPO on 30 September 2019 after its valuation collapsed from USD 47 billion to under USD 8 billion following governance concerns revealed in the S-1; SoftBank injected USD 9.5 billion to prevent collapse.

Tesla was added to the S&P 500 on 21 December 2020 at a market cap of USD 659 billion, one of the largest additions in the index's history. TSLA shares surged ~70 % in the two months preceding the inclusion date.
source_ref: S&P Dow Jones Indices Nov 2020; Reuters

description: Retail investors coordinating on Reddit's WallStreetBets drove GameStop shares from USD 20 to USD 483 between 11 January and 28 January 2021, causing massive losses at short-selling hedge funds and triggering a DTCC margin call that briefly restricted trading.

subcategory: Hedge Fund Collapse / Prime Brokerage Loss
description: Family office Archegos Capital collapsed in late March 2021 when its highly leveraged positions (via total-return swaps) were forcibly unwound by prime brokers, causing Credit Suisse and Nomura losses exceeding USD 10 billion and triggering a global media-stock sell-off.

Crypto exchange FTX filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on 11 November 2022 following the collapse of its native token FTT and revelations of misuse of customer funds. Bitcoin fell to USD 15,500 and crypto market cap lost over USD 200 billion within a week.

Microsoft completed its USD 68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard on 13 October 2023 after securing regulatory clearances from the UK CMA and other jurisdictions following nearly two years of antitrust battles.

event_name: Apple Becomes First USD 3 Trillion Market Cap Company
description: Apple became the first publicly traded company to reach a USD 3 trillion market capitalisation on 29 June 2023, closing above that level and reflecting sustained investor confidence in its services revenue growth.

event_name: Exxon Mobil Acquires Pioneer Natural Resources
description: Exxon Mobil announced the acquisition of Pioneer Natural Resources for USD 59.5 billion on 11 October 2023, the company's largest deal since the Mobil merger in 1998 and the largest oil-sector deal in decades.

event_name: Sam Altman Fired and Rehired at OpenAI
description: OpenAI's board abruptly fired CEO Sam Altman on 17 November 2023; following an employee revolt and Microsoft backing, Altman was reinstated as CEO five days later. The episode briefly threatened Microsoft's USD 13 billion investment and AI partnership.

event_name: Nvidia Blowout Earnings – AI Supercycle Catalyst
description: Nvidia reported Q1 FY2024 earnings on 24 May 2023 with revenue guidance of USD 11 billion (vs. USD 7.2 billion consensus), driven by AI-chip demand. NVDA surged ~24 % the following session, adding ~USD 184 billion in market cap.
source_ref: Nvidia Earnings Release Q1 FY2024; Reuters 2023-05-25

description: Pfizer and BioNTech announced on 9 November 2020 that their COVID-19 vaccine candidate showed over 90 % efficacy in Phase 3 trials. The S&P 500 surged ~1.2 %; travel, energy, and financial stocks outperformed sharply while stay-at-home stocks like Zoom fell.

Elon Musk completed the USD 44 billion acquisition of Twitter on 27 October 2022 and immediately began major restructuring, including laying off ~50 % of staff; Tesla shares fell on concerns about Musk's divided attention and the leveraged nature of the deal.
